# Introduction 




## Installing Packages


::: {.cell}

```{.bash .cell-code}
install.packages("devtools")
install.packages("usethis")
```
:::


## Create Package


::: {.cell}

```{.bash .cell-code}
library(usethis)
create_package('~/Documents/siliconPackage')
```
:::


## Create file


::: {.cell}

```{.bash .cell-code}
library(usethis)
use_r('silicon')
```
:::



## Package vs R Script

In normal R Scripts you call libraries but in a package you track dependencies differently with using `use_package()` which adds the package to the DESCRIPTION file. 


::: {.cell}

```{.bash .cell-code}
use_package('ggplot2')
```
:::


By default, r looks for function inside your own package first so we do not explicitly state the package name. But for external packages like `ggplot2` we would use `ggplot2::function`

### .Rprofile

With an .Rprofile file we can add libraries that should be loaded after opening the Package Project in R


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
if (!require(devtools)) {
  install.packages("devtools")
  library(devtools)
}
```
:::



## Do Checks 


::: {.cell}

```{.bash .cell-code}
devtools::check()
```
:::


## Publish on Github
First init git with `use_git('init package')`



::: {.cell}

```{.bash .cell-code}
use_github()
#or 
use_github('NameOfOrganization')
```
:::


## Download Package


::: {.cell}

```{.bash .cell-code}
devtools::install_github('username/packagename')
```
:::


## Documentation

Roxygen2 is a way of documenting function and with `@export` we tell roxygen2 that this function is ready for export and is accessible for other users that load the package. We can also call the usual `?function` the returns our short description. 
Other function **without** `@export` are internal function and can't be accessed. 

::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
#' Title
#' 
#' Short description of function with *markdown* syntax
#' 
#' @export
function_name <- function(){
  
}
```
:::


To make the documentation call the following in the console: 


::: {.cell}

```{.bash .cell-code}
devtools::document()
```
:::



::: {.cell}

```{.bash .cell-code}
use_mit_license()
```

## Test created functions 


::: {.cell}

```{.bash .cell-code}
use_testthat()

use_test('nameOfRRcript')

test()
```
:::


Alternatively in RStudio we can use `Build` to run all tests.


## Rename file 


::: {.cell}

```{.bash .cell-code}
rename_file('old', 'new')
```
:::


## Add readme for github


::: {.cell}

```{.bash .cell-code}
use_readme_rmd()
build_readme()
```
:::
